title: YUM (Yellowdog Updater, Modified)
definition: The traditional package manager used by older Red Hat-based distributions (like CentOS 7 and RHEL 7). It manages `.rpm` software packages.
simpleExplanation: The App Store for older Enterprise servers. It does exactly the same job as `apt`, just on a different brand of Linux.
realWorldExample: An administrator logs into a legacy CentOS 7 server and types `sudo yum install httpd` to install the Apache web server.

basic: Can you use the `yum` command on an Ubuntu server?

answers.question: Use on Ubuntu?
answers.answer: No. Ubuntu uses Debian architecture (`.deb` packages and `apt`). `yum` only works on Red Hat architecture.

answers.question: What is an .rpm file?
answers.answer: Red Hat Package Manager file. It is the compressed installation file (similar to a Windows `.msi`) that `yum` downloads and extracts.
